messages:
Elena (Sales): Sam from ACME ran into SSO + SCIM errors while onboarding the POC. Can we triage? ticket #POC-2345
Raj (SE): Thanks — tagging infra & security. Sam, what exact errors are you seeing when you try to provision?
Sam (ACME IT): SCIM: "401 SCIM token invalid". SAML: "Audience mismatch" when I test the SSO login. I uploaded a screenshot to the ticket.
Raj (SE): Ok. Two common things: 1) SCIM token mismatch if the token was generated for a different environment (host vs private). 2) Audience mismatch usually means the SP EntityID in Okta doesn't match the value in our metadata.
Marta (Infra): Sam, are you pointing Okta at the hosted endpoint or the VPC endpoint we gave you? For this POC we spun up the private-poc host: https://private-poc.redwood-inference.com
Sam (ACME IT): We used the URL from the quickstart (looks hosted). In the ticket you sent me a VPC URL earlier — not sure which one to use.
Raj (SE): If you're testing against the Dedicated/VPC POC, you must use the VPC endpoints and the SCIM token generated from that POC workspace. Hosted tokens won't work with the VPC base URL.
Sam (ACME IT): Understood. Where do I get the VPC SCIM token in the console?
Marta (Infra): Console -> POCs -> select "ACME POC" -> Integration -> SCIM -> Generate Token. Make sure you copy it once (we don't show it again). Also set the SCIM Base URL in Okta to: https://private-poc.redwood-inference.com/scim/v2
Raj (SE): For SAML, check the SP Entity ID in the Okta app configuration. It needs to match the value from our metadata endpoint: https://private-poc.redwood-inference.com/saml/metadata/ACME
Sam (ACME IT): Got a snippet from the Okta debugger: Assertion: Audience "https://api.redwood.io/" but our SP is the private-poc URL. That explains the mismatch.
James (Security): Quick security note: SCIM tokens for POCs are scoped to the workspace and expire at POC end. Do not reuse hosted creds. Also we've limited SCIM to user.read, user.write scope only — no groups.
okta-bot: SCIM test request: POST /scim/v2/Users -> 401 Bearer token invalid
Marta (Infra): Sounds like two fixes: 1) Regenerate SCIM token from the ACME POC workspace and update Okta's Bearer authorization header. 2) Replace the SP Entity ID/Audience in Okta with the private metadata URL Raj linked.
Sam (ACME IT): Regenerated token and updated base URL + audience. Running a test now...
okta-bot: SCIM test request: POST /scim/v2/Users -> 201 Created
Sam (ACME IT): Login SSO test also succeeded. 👍
Raj (SE): Great. Follow-up: I updated the POC checklist doc with explicit steps for Hosted vs VPC tokens and added a troubleshooting snippet for "Audience mismatch".
Elena (Sales): Thanks team — I'll update the customer-facing email and mark the blocker cleared in the CRM.
James (Security): I'll file a short note in the POC security checklist: remind customers to use workspace-scoped tokens and that SCIM is user-only for POCs.
Marta (Infra): I'll add an automated validation to the POC provisioning script to verify token scope and warn if the SP Entity ID doesn't match the POC metadata URL.
Sam (ACME IT): All good from our side. Appreciate the quick help.
Elena (Sales): Closing thread — will follow up if ACME requests a longer retention or group sync in next phase. :party-parrot:
